protocol.title: The Pomeranian and the bone
protocol.feedback: One conditional execution repair, no aesthetic feedback
protocol.servingVariants: Standard preferred; one model/version, no Fast duplicate
protocol.visualScoring: Qualitative film inspection; no automatic aesthetic points or local review form
protocol.infrastructureFailure: Unavailable, never a fabricated rendering failure or zero aesthetic score
protocol.capture: Offline isolated Chromium; actual viewport screenshots, not model telemetry; deterministic offline capture encoded at 30 fps
protocol.outputLimitPolicy: 32768 requested; GPT-4o and GPT-4o mini provider maximum 16384
protocol.thinkingPolicy: Low where supported; Haiku optional thinking disabled; native settings otherwise
protocol.subject: Pomeranian

calibration.note: An earlier high-reasoning budget calibration is retained privately and excluded from this gallery. Historical fox generation is retained separately. Current results use the identical initial task with the declared conditional repair policy; no best-of selection. Per-model calibration tokens and spend are disclosed separately.

methodology: Results use direct Microsoft Foundry and Google Vertex AI APIs. Private service configuration is excluded from the published dataset.

One unique model/version; Standard preferred over Fast. One initial response each. The same conditional execution repairs and recorded completion extension are available to every model. Final output is retained, never best-of. All known protocol response usage is included. Organizer setup calibration and recovered infrastructure replays are metered separately in billing data and excluded from comparison costs. No tools or reference artwork.

Identical initial prompt bytes. Truncated candidates can receive a separately labelled 65536-token completion rescue with a longer generation deadline; these are extended-budget results, not equal-budget comparisons. All rescue usage is included. The output allowance and reasoning setting are recorded per model; provider endpoint ceilings apply. Tokens include reasoning.

Actual model HTML runs only inside a separate offline Chromium process. Only recorded pixels and static evidence reach this catalog origin. Candidate HTML is provided as a text download, never executed by the website.

Every captured frame is a real 960×540 browser screenshot at a supplied timeline time. Video encodes 360 frames at 30 fps; it is deterministic offline capture, not a wall-clock performance demonstration.
Technical checks are diagnostics, not a visual quality score or proof of animal anatomy, correct reflections or foot contact. Visual expectations are provided to every model before generation.
The actual film is the visual result. No automatic aesthetic score or local rating form is published.

Price is an estimate from the dated official API rate snapshot, not a provider invoice. Regional adjustments, tax, promotional credit eligibility and billing differences can affect actual spend. Tokens come from terminal provider usage; reasoning is not counted twice.
